instructions.cross_packet_rule: Use cross_packet_terms for likely synonyms, owners, consumers, and seams outside this packet.
instructions.family_key_rule: Every assigned raw family key must have exactly one family_key_assignments row and at least one mapped feature.
instructions.objective: Normalize every assigned validated audit atom into an exhaustive local inventory of distinct Puppet Master features, systems, tools, workflows, GUI surfaces, integrations, data models, governance controls, or cross-cutting concerns. Preserve under-specification, contradictions, unknowns, and explicit non-gaps.
instructions.output_rule: Write exactly one strict-schema JSON payload in the assigned output directory and then return PMR1.
instructions.partition_rule: Every atom_id must appear in exactly one feature.atom_ids array; no omission or duplication.
instructions.research_rule: Do not browse in this phase. Give every normalized feature at least one concrete external-research question for the mandatory next phase; do not treat absence of seed queries as permission to omit research.
instructions.scenario_rule: Give every feature at least one falsifiable scenario requirement for later certification.
instructions.split_merge_rule: Split concepts with distinct lifecycle, authority, consumers, or failure semantics. Merge only true synonyms describing the same product concept; record aliases and relationships instead of collapsing uncertainty.

atoms.statement: The Markdown file is a template/example owner, while the schema-validated production matrix and its exclusions artifact are the current production wiring authority.
atoms.title: Template prose and production JSON authority are explicitly separated

atoms.statement: A production row is more than a command-to-handler edge: it includes typed selection, disabled-state projection, effect, accessibility, test, and evidence obligations.
atoms.title: Production rows have typed state, effect, accessibility, and evidence contracts

atoms.statement: The canonical seven-column template omits the typed state selector, disabled reason, effect, accessibility, test evidence, and event-test requirements that the later production contract says are mandatory.
atoms.title: Base template and example shape lag the production row contract

atoms.statement: Approval is bound to all displayed planning revisions and hashes; stale input fails closed, success atomically records approval and compile binding, and identical retries return the same PlanCompileRun.
atoms.title: Approve And Build has strong CAS, atomicity, and idempotency oracles

atoms.statement: The contract says the compile view opens as a pending-launch or durable-run projection, but it does not define the user-visible state, retry key, or reconciliation behavior if the atomic approval succeeds and opening or projecting the compile run fails.
atoms.title: Post-approval projection failure has no explicit recovery outcome

atoms.statement: Testing readiness spans inherited Auto/On/Off policy, visible browser and native streams, open/watch controls, redaction before display or persistence, disabled reasons, and background execution.
atoms.title: Visible testing wiring includes policy projection, streams, redaction, and background continuation

atoms.statement: Every retained production control must bind accessible name, role, keyboard behavior, state attributes, disabled reason, command, handler, events, and evidence, with zero unnamed or keyboard-inaccessible actions.

atoms.statement: The otherwise exhaustive production-control evidence chain does not bind string identity, locale-aware formatting, expansion/overflow behavior, translated disabled reasons, or bidirectional layout behavior.

atoms.statement: The gate requires every catalog command to appear in production but does not equivalently state that every production command must resolve to a canonical catalog identity; exclusion creation also lacks owner, reason, expiry, and approval criteria.

atoms.statement: Existence of a callable path and exact emitted event names does not prove handler signature compatibility, input validation, permission enforcement, effect/state-selector agreement, or the state transition of rows with no events.

atoms.statement: The gate boundary names `allowed_action_ids` and `allowed_action_ids[]`, but the handler rule later keys handlers by an `allowed_action_id` family; the document never defines whether a blocked payload carries one action, a list, or both normalized forms.

atoms.title: Compose and scenario command family

atoms.statement: Every compose/scenario command requires a receipt or explicit no-persist disposition and forbids unexpected persisted domain events.
atoms.title: Receipt-only effect contract is explicit

atoms.statement: Delete and down operations are wired but lack confirmation, authorization, affected-resource scope, dependency handling, retention, undo, rollback, and invalid-state rules.
atoms.title: Destructive compose operations lack safety semantics

atoms.statement: Scenario edit/save/run commands do not define scenario schema identity, revision preconditions, optimistic concurrency, atomicity, idempotency, partial-save recovery, or version migration.
atoms.title: Scenario consistency and migration rules are absent

atoms.statement: This window defines compose-up controls plus container navigation, shell attachment, deletion, inspection, and open operations.
atoms.title: Container operation capability set

atoms.statement: The attach-shell control explicitly requires stable accessible naming, keyboard activation, visible focus, deterministic focus return, and disabled-reason announcement.
atoms.title: Container control accessibility is testable

atoms.statement: Container deletion has a receipt-only effect but no confirmation, resource identity precondition, volume/data-loss warning, authorization rule, concurrent-state guard, persisted audit outcome, or recovery contract.
atoms.title: Container deletion lacks safety and recovery contract

atoms.statement: Attach shell lacks a defined principal and privilege boundary, command/input trust model, terminal encoding and escape policy, secret/redaction lifecycle, session termination, backpressure, and disconnect semantics.
atoms.title: Attach-shell security and session lifecycle are undefined

atoms.statement: The visible Docker Manager consumes commands for restart, stats, stop, logs, context selection, and repository creation.
atoms.title: Docker Manager is the declared command consumer

atoms.statement: Restart and stop are named as commands but the legal source states, transitional states, terminal states, duplicate-dispatch behavior, race resolution, timeout, rollback, and reconnect reconciliation are not defined.
atoms.title: Container restart and stop transition model is absent

atoms.statement: Stats and log commands lack snapshot-versus-stream semantics, sampling or ordering, pagination/backpressure, retention, redaction, maximum volume, disconnect indication, resumption, and stale-data presentation rules.
atoms.title: Stats and logs lack streaming, privacy, and scale contracts

atoms.statement: Context selection and repository creation do not define input schemas, context identity and persistence, credential ownership, name validation, authorization, conflict handling, atomicity, retry/idempotency, offline failure, or compatibility behavior.
atoms.title: Context selection and repository creation remain underspecified

atoms.statement: Window 26 applies a production wiring envelope to cancel, confirm, drift compare, exec, host-access, and host-restart controls: dispatcher typing, state and disabled projections, a receipt or event effect, accessibility behavior, and named test evidence are required.
atoms.title: Window 26 defines a uniform production wiring envelope

atoms.statement: The restart oracle names the shared lifecycle event and correlation metadata, but the assigned unit does not expose an event payload field that identifies restart or a state-machine oracle for its precondition and completion transition.
atoms.title: Restart lifecycle semantics stop at event identity

atoms.statement: The complete window supplies generic typed args/results and dispatch evidence but does not specify authorization scope, target validation, idempotency or concurrency policy, partial-failure states, or rollback/recovery behavior for Docker exec and restart.
atoms.title: Privileged exec and restart lack safety semantics

atoms.statement: Window 27 binds each host action to a handler, state projections, a declared event effect, and an event test carrying command, origin, correlation, and handler-target evidence.
atoms.title: Host actions have explicit event-backed dispatch behavior

atoms.statement: Start and stop deliberately share docker.host.instance_lifecycle_requested, while the unit provides no legal-state table, operation discriminator, mutual-exclusion rule, completion/failure events, or race-resolution oracle.
atoms.title: Start and stop lack lifecycle race and completion oracles

atoms.statement: The retention and profile-save entries prove event emission and correlation, but their complete assigned definitions do not bind retention duration/deletion semantics, profile data classification, secret treatment, migration behavior, or caller authority.
atoms.title: Retention and profile data lifecycle remains cross-document

atoms.statement: Window 28 explicitly defines a multi-part production-certification oracle for host refresh/session/route and image controls, including render, dispatch, typed contract, projected state, disabled reason, effect, accessibility, and regression proof.
atoms.title: Window 28 certification requires executable UI and dispatch evidence

atoms.statement: Image delete is explicitly receipt-only and must emit no unexpected persisted event, yet its assigned definition contains no destructive confirmation, authority, dependency check, rollback, recovery, or external-state reconciliation contract.
atoms.title: Image delete is receipt-only without destructive-action safeguards

atoms.statement: Host session launch declares a request event and dispatch metadata but no authorization boundary, session-parameter validation, success/failure transition, disconnect cleanup, offline behavior, or session-closure evidence in the assigned unit.
atoms.title: Host session launch lacks authority and terminal lifecycle contracts

atoms.statement: Window 29 intentionally classifies image push/tag/inspect and Kubernetes apply/diff/exec as receipt-or-disposition effects with a negative oracle forbidding unexpected persisted domain events.
atoms.title: Receipt-only effects are explicit rather than missing wiring

atoms.statement: The explicit receipt-only classification for image push and Kubernetes apply is not paired with an oracle for the lifecycle of their external side effects, including partial completion, retries, rollback, and eventual reconciliation.
atoms.title: External mutations have dispatch receipts but no completion recovery model

atoms.statement: Kubernetes apply and exec require typed args/results, but the assigned definitions do not expose payload fields or constraints for untrusted manifests/commands, target authorization, credentials, privilege boundaries, or sensitive output.
atoms.title: Kubernetes apply and exec omit payload security boundaries

atoms.statement: Window 30 consistently binds its visible Helm, logs, port-forward, context, namespace, and Docker-log controls to keyboard, focus, semantic naming, and disabled-announcement evidence.
atoms.title: Window 30 makes accessibility and disabled truth certifiable

atoms.statement: Helm install is explicitly receipt-only, while its assigned entry contains no release transaction state, idempotency key, atomicity boundary, partial-failure result, rollback operation, timeout behavior, or final cluster-state oracle.
atoms.title: Helm install lacks transactional and rollback semantics

atoms.statement: Port forward has typed dispatch and an opening receipt but no exposed bind/interface rule, target authorization, lifecycle state, cancellation command, offline transition, cleanup guarantee, or closure evidence.
atoms.title: Port forward lacks exposure controls and terminal cleanup

atoms.statement: Context and namespace selection define availability and disabled projections plus receipt effects, but not the selected-value state owner, success transition, downstream propagation, stale-target invalidation, persistence/migration rule, or UI truth after failure.
atoms.title: Context and namespace selection lack authoritative state propagation

atoms.statement: Kubernetes logs and Docker logs define receipt-only dispatch wiring but no data classification/redaction, untrusted-output rendering, retention, stream termination, scale limits, pagination/backpressure, truncation, or localized timestamp contract.
atoms.title: Log commands omit privacy, untrusted-output, and scale semantics

atoms.statement: Each catalog entry binds a UI element and command to a handler, projected availability and disabled reason, a typed dispatcher/result assertion, an explicit receipt effect, accessibility behavior, and production evidence.
atoms.title: Docker catalog wiring contract is structurally explicit

atoms.statement: The destructive and lifecycle-changing Docker commands are wired only to generic receipt and availability contracts, leaving their safety transitions and failure semantics unspecified.
atoms.title: Docker lifecycle actions lack destructive-state safeguards

atoms.statement: The registry promote and tag-push entries provide generic typed dispatch and receipt evidence but no network, credential, remote-authority, or partial-transfer contract.
atoms.title: Registry operations omit remote failure and credential boundaries

atoms.statement: Docker show, stop, subview, volume, and file copy commands retain the common typed-dispatch, state-projection, receipt, and accessibility test structure.
atoms.title: Window preserves common command certification structure

atoms.statement: Docker stop and volume are modeled as receipt-only dispatches without a falsifiable asynchronous lifecycle or recovery contract.
atoms.title: Docker stop and volume lack operation lifecycle states

atoms.statement: The file copy commands specify dispatch receipts but omit the output destination, clipboard lifecycle, privacy boundary, and precise copy_nodes state semantics.
atoms.title: File copy commands leave clipboard and data-lifecycle behavior undefined

atoms.statement: File delete, new-file, and new-folder commands declare concrete success events and event tests, while non-persisting commands retain explicit receipt contracts.
atoms.title: Mutating file commands declare success-event correlation

atoms.statement: The delete wiring proves only a correlated success event and does not define the destructive action's preconditions, failure partitioning, or recovery semantics.
atoms.title: File deletion has no recoverability or partial-failure contract

atoms.statement: New-file and new-folder success events are specified, but input validation, collision policy, platform compatibility, concurrency, and failure cleanup are not.
atoms.title: File creation omits naming, collision, and atomicity rules

atoms.statement: The system-default open command stops at typed dispatch and a receipt, without defining the external-application security and failure boundary.
atoms.title: System-default file opening lacks an untrusted-input boundary

atoms.statement: File and Git entries preserve typed dispatch, projected availability, disabled copy, correlated effects, accessibility assertions, and regression evidence.
atoms.title: File and Git entries retain correlated production wiring

atoms.statement: Several filesystem-changing commands are treated as receipt-only operations even though their effects require mutation, partial-failure, and recovery semantics.
atoms.title: Paste and save-copy mutations are modeled as receipts only

atoms.statement: Git conflict resolution is modeled as a receipt-only command despite changing repository state, with no state transition or consumer propagation contract.
atoms.title: Conflict resolution lacks repository-state propagation

atoms.statement: Open-with has generic typed dispatch and receipt evidence but no normative external-program selection or untrusted-input contract.
atoms.title: Open-with omits external program and argument safety

atoms.statement: Git diff, alias, discard, stage, and unstage commands use typed dispatcher/state/accessibility evidence and explicit receipts, while aliases are required to normalize to canonical command language.
atoms.title: Git receipts reject placeholder events and aliases normalize

atoms.statement: Discard-hunks has only generic dispatch and receipt assertions despite being a destructive repository transition.
atoms.title: Discard hunks has no confirmation, stale-target, or recovery contract

atoms.statement: Stage-hunks and unstage-hunks are receipt-only despite mutating shared Git index state and requiring downstream source-control propagation.
atoms.title: Stage and unstage lack index-state propagation and race handling

atoms.statement: The open-diff alias is required to normalize to the canonical command but retains alias-specific state and receipt identifiers without an explicit end-to-end equivalence oracle.
atoms.title: Compatibility aliases can drift from canonical command state

cross_document_questions: Where are typed payload and result fields, authorization rules, and error variants for these Docker, file, and Git commands canonically defined?
Which canonical state owner consumes file and Git mutation effects and refreshes file-tree, diff, status, and commit-readiness projections after success, partial failure, cancellation, or rollback?
What document defines destructive-action confirmation, undo or recovery, stale-target rejection, and partial-operation policy for file deletion and hunk discard?
What compatibility contract proves alias and canonical commands share payload normalization, availability, disabled reason, handler result, receipt, telemetry, and accessibility semantics?
